text:
maria-gomez: Heads up, nightly perf regression on the 2.1.0 autopicker run. Median latency up ~18% for mid-length requests (seqlen 128-512).
raj-patel: ugh. same regression window as the kernel selector change last week?
leo-wang: yes, saw the same in local replay. It looks like the selector is preferring the tiled-attn path for those shapes now.
sarah-choi: tiled-attn usually better for long seqs, not mid. Could be launch overhead vs batch shape mix.
maria-gomez: attached flame trace from perf-bot shows a lot more time in kernel_handshake and dev_launch for those batches. perf-bot, can you paste the graph?
perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/2065432100/flame.svg — increased time in LaunchAndHandshake and kernel_probe.
leo-wang: I replayed with tagging: when continuous-batching is enabled and batch sizes fluctuate between 8 and 20, the selector jumps to tiled path because peak-seq heuristic sees a few long sequences in the batch. That makes sense algorithmically but hurts median due to launch cost.
raj-patel: so the problem is selector uses a max-seqlen heuristic + kernel latency table, but ignores launch-overhead amortization. autotuner should account for expected batch composition and launch probability.
sarah-choi: agreed. Quick fix: lower the tiled path threshold for the autotuner for Ampere in mid-seqlen range. But we should add a launch_penalty term to the cost model.
maria-gomez: i ran a variant: set launch_penalty_ms=0.6 in kernel_cost_config and retested — median latency dropped back ~10% but p99 still slightly worse. Command I ran:
```
redwoodctl runtime test --model=gpt-medium --shape=128-512 --config override:{"kernel_cost_config":{"launch_penalty_ms":0.6}}
```
leo-wang: can we get KV cache warmup in the replay? I suspect handshake + KV population interacts: early tokens hit empty KV causing more small launches.
perf-bot: replay run with KV warmup enabled: https://perf.internal/runs/2065432120/compare — shows reduced dev_launch frequency.
raj-patel: good find. Two orthogonal fixes: 1) improve cost model (add launch_penalty + batch-distribution weighting) 2) tweak continuous-batcher to avoid mixing long tails with short requests when possible.
sarah-choi: for (1) I'll add a weighted expectation calculation: E[launch_cost] = p_long*launch_penalty + p_short*0, where p_long is probability of at least one long seq in batch (computed from recent histogram).
maria-gomez: is there a cheap way to estimate p_long online? We could use exponential moving average of seqlen histogram per serving shard.
leo-wang: yep, EMAs per length bucket is cheap and already collected in telemetry. I'll prototype and run autotune sweep.
perf-bot: autotune sweep started: https://perf.internal/autotune/2065432145 — will test launch_penalty in {0,0.3,0.6,1.0} and tiled_threshold shifts.
deploy-bot: Canary queued: kernel-cost-model-v2 on pool-gamma (5% traffic) at 2065432180.
raj-patel: canary will confirm real traffic behavior. If we still see median regressions, roll back. Keep an eye on tail.
sarah-choi: also adding a guard: if recent batch variance > 0.35, bias selector towards low-launch kernels. That should reduce oscillation.
maria-gomez: timeline? can we have a PR with cost-model + ema buckets today, run full replay tonight?
leo-wang: i'll push draft PR in ~2h and link perf results.
raj-patel: curious — do we need to change kernel compilation heuristics too (different kernel variants for mid-seq sizes)? or just selector weighting?
sarah-choi: short-term selector weighting + batcher tweak. Longer term we might add a mid-sized kernel variant optimized for amortized launch. Add issue in board.
maria-gomez: created issue: https://boards.internal/INFR-984 "selector: include launch amortization & EMA seqlen" with notes.
perf-bot: summary snapshot: before: median=122ms, after (launch_penalty=0.6 + kv-warmup)=106ms, p99 from 420ms -> 390ms. Canary will reveal production mix effects.
leo-wang: thanks. I'll watch the canary and if things look good we'll promote and roll out autotuner changes. :thumbsup:
raj-patel: thanks team — nice narrow triage on a subtle interaction (batch variance x kernel pick x KV warmup).
maria-gomez: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after canary stabilizes. :white_check_mark:
